reason: A: the bottle is a tiny sliver jammed against the left edge, the Lumen & Fig logo has shrunk to an unreadable dot, the leaf imagery is lost, the 'NEW NIGHT SERUM' eyebrow has dropped below the body copy, and the oversized CTA overpowers the headline across a large dead gap in the middle. B: it keeps the leaf panel, the bottle and a legible logo, with a clear headline → body → CTA flow that reads left to right, but the bottle is small, the logo and eyebrow are tiny and pushed below the body copy, and the CTA sits tight to the right edge.

A reads well as a left-to-right banner: a large jar, then the headline block, then the CTA. But the NEW badge has shrunk to a tiny sticker floating above the headline, and the CTA is stranded far right with a wide gap. In B the jar is shrunk and pushed close to the left edge, and the illegible NEW badge sits below the subcopy, which breaks reading order and separates it from the product. A large dead zone also sits between the text and the CTA.

A reads well as a left-to-right banner: the jar is a strong hero and the headline is clearly dominant. However, the NEW badge is squashed into a flat ellipse and floats on its own above the headline instead of sitting with the product. Shop Now sits high on the right and doesn't line up with the headline, leaving empty space bottom-right. B shrinks the jar so far that the LUMEN & FIG label can't be read, and the NEW badge becomes a tiny orphan below the subcopy, which breaks the reading order. The headline is crammed against the small jar while the centre-right is a large dead gap, so the product looks trivial.

A: the stack is sensible, but there is about 85px of empty space above the NEW badge and about 85px below the CTA. The jar is shrunk to a small mid-column object, and the subcopy breaks awkwardly as 'Whipped fig and / shea, $38'. B: the product, headline and subcopy are larger and easier to read, the line break is better ('Whipped fig / and shea, $38') and the CTA reads clearly. However, the NEW badge is shrunk and jammed into the top-left corner, far from the jar, and a large empty band remains below the button, so the layout feels top-heavy.

A: the cream jar is cut off from the serum and dumped as an orphan at the bottom under the CTA, 'THE NIGHT SET' eyebrow has fallen below its own copy, and the logo jams into the circle; still, $48 dominates and everything sits on a centred axis. B has the same orphaned jar but pushed off-axis to the bottom-left, a tiny logo shoved into the top-right corner, a smaller $48, the 'Worth $72' line set larger than the product description (inverted hierarchy), and a widowed 'wash.' line.

A breaks the reading order. The CTA floats alone at the top left above a cropped leaf strip. The 'Clinically Tested' eyebrow has dropped below the subhead. The product jar is shrunk to an unreadable thumbnail in the corner, the legal text is microscopic, and the logo sits stranded at the bottom centre. B keeps the original's image-left, copy-right structure and the headline hierarchy. Its flaws: the CTA sits above the headline instead of after it, the eyebrow sits below the subcopy, the legal text is tiny and jammed under the copy block, and the logo is oversized next to a small jar, so the bottom cluster is crowded.

A: the reading order and date card survive. But the layout is scattered: big dead gaps separate the eyebrow, headline, body and a tiny CTA; the date card floats alone on the left; the headphones have come off their grey circle, which now sits as a stray blob in the bottom-right corner. B: the headline is strong and fills the width, but the order is jumbled: the CTA sits above the headline and the 'LISTENING SESSION' eyebrow falls below the body copy. The date card has shrunk to a tiny chip with 'FRI, 7:30 PM' unreadable. The grey circle is cut away from the headphones and collides with the right earcup.

A: the price is reversed to '$3' over '2 FOR', the CTA is moved to the top-right corner, and the right-column text is ragged: '$3', '2 FOR' and the body copy all start at different x positions. The $3 is too small to dominate, and the FIZZBANG! logo floats on its own near the bottom, aligned with nothing. B: the same '$3' over '2 FOR' reversal and top-placed CTA, plus a big dead gap between '$3' and '2 FOR', and the logo shrinks to a barely legible pill. Even so, B's column shares one centre axis and the $3 is a strong focal point, so it is slightly less broken.

A breaks the event information: the yellow date card is shrunk to an unreadable speck in the top-right, the body copy is tiny in the top-left corner above the headline, the 'FIZZBANG ARCADE NIGHT' eyebrow is pushed to the very bottom out of reading order, the controller is a scrap in the bottom-left corner, and a huge blow-up of the decorative pattern dominates the middle of the canvas. B is a coherent centred stack (logo, headline, date, copy, CTA) that keeps the brand intact, but the date card is too small so SAT/NOV/8PM-1AM are unreadable, the eyebrow sits below the body copy instead of above the headline, the pattern strip is a cropped sliver, and the controller is shrunk to a token icon.

A: the yellow date card shrinks to an unreadable speck at the bottom, the venue line and 'FIZZBANG ARCADE NIGHT' eyebrow are tiny and sit below the CTA, the controller is pushed into a corner, and a huge cropped pattern block takes over the middle as the main visual, so the date and the reading order are lost. B: better order and the venue line is readable, but the date card is still too small (SAT/NOV/8PM–1AM can't be read), the eyebrow ends up below the body copy, and the pattern strip and controller are scaled down to a thin band and a small icon with uneven gaps.

A shrinks the can to a tiny icon at the bottom, which loses the key product image. It puts the CTA top-right ahead of the headline, so the reading order is wrong. It reorders the flavour list (Mango and Cola before Grape and Lime) and leaves wide empty side margins around a narrow centred column. B uses a sensible banner layout: a large can on the left, then headline, list and a prominent CTA on the right. But the FIZZBANG! logo is shrunk to a near-illegible badge stranded in the bottom-left corner, the list has the same reordering, and the text column is cramped against the right edge.

A swaps the reading order: the 'SINCE 2026' badge now sits above the FIZZBANG! pill, which breaks fidelity to the original's logo-then-tagline stack. Its oversized pill also runs within about 20px of the side edges, so the frame feels crowded and bottom-heavy. B keeps the original order and centred axis with even breathing room, but its badge is shrunk until the 'SINCE 2026' text is tiny and hard to read at 300x250, and the pill could be a little larger.

A rewraps the headline to three centred lines, sits it on the optical centre and leaves even side margins. It is faithful to the minimal original, though 'silence.' still runs close to the edges. B sets the type larger, so 'silence.' and 'follows' almost touch both canvas edges, and it pushes the block well below centre, leaving a big empty top against a cramped lower third.

A: the photo is cropped to a thin, meaningless strip at the top. The 'EXHIBITION' kicker has dropped below the address, so the reading order is broken. The logo is a microscopic mark in the bottom-left, and the left-hugging stack leaves dead space on the right. B: the headline is strong and the image stays prominent, but the address is promoted to the top. The date box is jammed onto the bottom of the photo, which looks like a collision rather than layering. The 'EXHIBITION' label and the logo have shrunk to illegible specks in the bottom-left corner. B is slightly less bad because its hierarchy and imagery hold up better.

Both demote the Monograph logo from a top masthead to a tiny footer mark where 'GALLERY' is illegible, and both move the $420 price above the 'Field Watch No. 2' name, which reverses the original reading order. A is worse: the logo sits off-axis in the bottom-left corner, breaking the centred layout, and there is a large empty band above the watch while the bottom is crowded. B keeps the logo on the centre axis and spaces the stack more evenly, but the shrunken logo is still a clear brand-fidelity flaw.

A: the Monograph logo is shrunk to a tiny, unreadable mark and left alone in the bottom-left corner, off the centred axis, so the brand is effectively lost. The price also sits above the product name, the reverse of the original, and wide empty side margins make it look like the tall layout dropped into a square. B: the logo is just as tiny and illegible but at least sits on the central axis, and the watch is larger, with tighter grouping. Its flaws are the same reversed price-over-name order, a product name that is now small and weak, and a logo below the CTA that reads as an afterthought.

Both break the reading order: the 'Plan a Visit' CTA is pushed to the top-left corner above the logo, and the 'NOW OPEN' eyebrow ends up below the body copy. A also drops the architectural photo entirely, wraps the headline into three cramped lines and jams 'NOW OPEN' against the bottom edge. B keeps a thin strip of the photo for some fidelity, but that strip is a meaningless fragment, 'NOW OPEN' is so big it competes with the headline, and the headline sits tight against the body copy.

A keeps the photo and the white card, but the oversized logo sits on the busy grey image and its 'MONOGRAPH' wordmark runs into the card edge, so the logo competes with the headline. 'NOW OPEN' drops below the body copy, the headline is jammed against the top edge, and 'GALLERY' is barely visible. B removes the architecture photo completely, so the design loses its key image and feel. It also flips the reading order: the CTA sits at the very top, the logo in the middle and the 'NOW OPEN' eyebrow at the bottom, leaving a plain white box that no longer reads as the same design.

A moves the headline above the watch and leaves an empty band about 100px tall at the top. It also swaps the price above the subhead and drops the logo from top-left to a small spot beside the legal text at the bottom, which weakens the brand and the original's product-then-message order. B keeps the original order of watch, headline and CTA and fills the canvas better. However, it also swaps the price and subhead, its upscaled watch looks soft and pixelated, and the CTA, demoted logo and tiny legal text are crammed together at the bottom.

A has a clean left-aligned stack (logo, headline, subline, CTA) with clear hierarchy, but it drops the sea photo entirely, which costs fidelity. The subline also runs almost to the right edge, and the headline breaks awkwardly, leaving '$89' on its own line. B squeezes the photo into a thin top strip, where the white logo sits on pale sky and is nearly invisible. It also leaves a large empty blue gap in the middle and crams all the copy against the bottom. The CTA is centred while the text above it is left-aligned, and the subline nearly touches both side edges.

Both swap the copy so it reads '$199 / New York / from', with 'from' after its price, which breaks the message. A also shrinks the Meridian logo to an illegible speck under 'from', so the brand is effectively lost, and it leaves dead space between the copy and the Book button. B keeps the logo at a readable size, but it shrinks 'from' to tiny text stuck beside the logo, crowds the logo against the suitcase wheels at the bottom, and the suitcase nearly touches the top and bottom edges. B is slightly less bad because the brand mark survives.

Both put '$199' above 'New York' and leave 'from' hanging after the city, so the copy now reads '$199 New York from'. A's Meridian logo is shrunk to an illegible speck under the text block, which wrecks the brand. Its suitcase also fills the full height with almost no top or bottom margin, and its 'Book' button is small. B's logo is still undersized, and it is parked at an arbitrary spot near the suitcase's bottom-right instead of on the text axis. But B's logo is readable, and its CTA is a little more substantial, so B is the less broken of the two.

A uses the space boldly, but the 'How It Works' CTA floats at the top right of the text column, above the headline and aligned with nothing, which breaks the reading order. The suitcase and its circle are cropped awkwardly at the bottom and right edges, and the legal text is shrunk to near-illegible micro type. B keeps the original order and hierarchy intact, but it is basically a shrunk, centred copy: a wide empty left margin, a small headline, dead space under the text block, and fine print that is too small to read.

A keeps the reading order (logo, headline, copy, CTA at the bottom) and the sky/sunglasses scene, but its logo is blown up and straddles the panel's top edge with white on pale sky (poor contrast), the badge is squashed into a flat tilted sliver stuck in the bottom-left, and the panel runs nearly to the right edge. B covers almost the whole canvas with the blue panel and loses the scenery; it also flips the reading order, with the squashed badge and the CTA crammed in a top strip above the logo, the sunglasses jammed into the corner, an oversized logo competing with the headline, an orphaned 'midnight.' and dead space in the middle.

A is the original pasted unchanged into the middle of a wider canvas: the blue header band stops short of both edges, leaving odd white strips, and the content has not been rearranged for the new shape. Even so, every element is intact, readable and in order. B is broken: the blue header covers the Vienna row, so the city name and the $109 price are cut off, the destination list has been reshuffled, the legal line now sits above the CTA, and the centred logo does not line up with the left-aligned headline.

A keeps the image-left/text-right split and a strong headline, but the CTA is put above the headline at top right, so the reading order is broken. The 'Clinically tested' eyebrow is moved below the subcopy and enlarged. The legal text is microscopic and the logo is so big it competes with the headline. The jar is shrunk and pulled out of the leaf image. B crops the leaves into a thin strip and floats the CTA above it, cut off from the copy. The jar is shrunk to an unreadable thumbnail at bottom left and the logo is small, and both are scattered along the bottom row with tiny unreadable legal text. The eyebrow again sits under the subcopy, and the product and brand presence are lost far more than in A.

A: the can/text split suits the format and the headline and CTA have a clear hierarchy. But the FIZZBANG! logo is shrunk to a tiny chip stuck in the bottom-left corner, which leaves the lower third mostly dead. The flavour list is also out of the original's order, and its small text is cramped against the right edge. B: the CTA sits top-right above the headline, which breaks the reading order. The can is shrunk to a trivial icon at the bottom, so the key product image is lost. The flavour list is out of order too, and the canvas has a crowded top and a weak, empty bottom.

A: the reading order is scrambled ($199 above New York), 'from' is shrunk to tiny type and stuck next to the logo as an orphan, the logo is pushed into the bottom corner of the copy block, and the suitcase handle is jammed against the top edge. B: the suitcase is framed better and the centre column is cleaner, but 'from' still sits after 'New York', below the price it should introduce, and the Meridian logo has shrunk to a barely legible speck, which badly weakens the brand.

Both scramble the reading order: '$199 / New York / from' now reads as nonsense when it should be 'New York from $199'. Both also run the suitcase almost edge to edge vertically, with a big empty gap between the text block and the Book button. A keeps a readable Meridian logo, but it is shrunk and stuck awkwardly in the bottom-left beside the suitcase wheels, lined up with nothing. B's logo is an illegible speck under the text, and its 'from' and Book button are tiny too, so the brand effectively disappears. That makes B the weaker of the two.

A is basically the original shrunk and centred. It leaves wide dead gutters on the left and right, the headline and CTA are small for the canvas, and the legal block is tiny, though the reading order and grouping stay intact. B fills the width better with a bold headline and a large suitcase. But it moves the CTA to the top right beside the logo, so the action comes before the headline and the reading order breaks. Its legal text is shrunk to an illegible size and jammed under the subhead, and the suitcase crowds the right edge.

A: the 'Shop the Duo' pill sits right against the headline's left edge, which puts the CTA before the message. 'duo' runs into the peach circle. The serum bottle has shrunk to a tiny icon stranded under the subcopy, so the duo is lost and the reading order is jumbled. B has no collisions and a clean headline/subcopy column, but the serum bottle is again shrunk to a meaningless speck. The CTA is oversized inside the circle and competes with the headline, and the jar on the left has been separated from its partner.

Both break the product duo: the serum bottle shrinks to a tiny stray icon in the bottom-left while the cream jar is blown up to dominate the canvas, and the peach circle sits on its own in the bottom-right corner as an empty blob. A is a little better because its headline, subcopy and CTA share one left edge and stay grouped, though its centred logo clashes with the left-aligned text and the serum is jammed under the CTA. B scatters everything: the logo is pushed oddly to the top-right, there is a large dead gap between the headline and subcopy, the centred CTA sits squeezed against the circle, and the serum is pressed against the bottom edge.

A keeps the original layout and hierarchy intact (badge, jar, headline, copy, CTA all in proportion). Its flaws are wide, inconsistent side margins (about 40px on the left), so the whole block sits inward, and a large empty right half next to the left-aligned copy. B distorts the NEW badge into a squashed flat ellipse and shrinks the hero jar to a tiny thumbnail stranded mid-canvas between the copy and the CTA. That leaves the right side dead and buries the product, so the design loses its key imagery.

A keeps a clean shared left edge for badge, headline, subcopy and CTA, but the 'Night Cream' headline and especially the subcopy are undersized for the canvas. The NEW badge is cut loose from the jar it overlapped in the original, and the big vertical gaps make the text column look sparse. B is worse: the CTA is offset right and doesn't line up with the headline/subcopy edge, and the NEW badge floats alone in the top-right corner. The headline, subcopy and button are spaced unevenly with large gaps, so the copy block falls apart and looks arbitrary.

A keeps the right hierarchy, with a large 'Lumen & Fig' lockup, but the circle is stretched into a cropped ellipse. 'Fig' straddles the ellipse's edge, and 'Skincare, slowly.' is jammed against the right canvas edge. B reverses the hierarchy: the brand lockup is shrunk to a tiny afterthought, pushed to the left edge and sitting half on the ellipse's border, while the tagline becomes the focal point. B also stretches the circle into an ellipse, so B is worse on brand and hierarchy.

A: the logo and wordmark are big and lead the layout as they should, but the 'g' in 'Fig' runs into the edge of the pink shape. The circle has been stretched into an oval and cut off at the top, bottom and right, which leaves the small tagline floating alone inside it. B: the logo and wordmark are shrunk and pushed against the left edge, so they lose to a large stretched oval in the centre that holds only the tagline. That flips the hierarchy, and the right third of the canvas is left as empty space.

A keeps the night-city backdrop and layers the headphones over the card, but the logo floats off-centre to the right, the 'OBSIDIAN ONE' eyebrow drops below the subcopy (wrong reading order), the headline runs almost to the card edge, and there is a dead gap between the headphones and the headline. B fills nearly the whole canvas with the card and leaves an odd sliver of city at the right edge, so the city imagery is lost. Its dark headphones sink into the dark card with little contrast, the logo is centred while the headline and the CTA are left-aligned (mixed alignment), and the eyebrow again sits below the subcopy.

A loses both products: the headphones are gone and the earbud case shows only as stray dots in the bottom-left. 'PICK YOUR SOUND' sits below the headline and body, out of reading order, and the price labels float with nothing to label, with the Buds label colliding with a leftover shadow ellipse beside the CTA. B keeps the headphones, but the 'Obsidian One, $349' label sits in the text column, larger than the body copy and away from its product. The eyebrow is still below the subhead, the Buds label is tiny and jammed against the CTA, the earbud case is clipped at the bottom edge, the logo is pushed to the bottom-left, and there is a large empty dark area at the lower right. Both fail, and B is less bad only because it keeps some of the key imagery.

A: the 'Pick your sound' eyebrow sits below the headline and under the floating 'Obsidian One, $349' caption, so the reading order is jumbled. The logo sits on a stray dark blob, and the buds case is cramped against the bottom edge and cut off. It does keep a large headphone image and a readable CTA. B: the hierarchy is inverted. The body copy and the price caption are nearly as big as the headline, the eyebrow is oversized and placed below everything, and the CTA is shrunk to a tiny button wedged next to an unreadable 'Obsidian Buds, $179' pill. The buds product is reduced to a speck, which leaves the bottom cluttered and weak.

A: the reading order is scrambled. The 'Find a Store' CTA sits at the top above '$3', and '2 FOR' falls below the price. The FIZZBANG logo has shrunk to an unreadable speck at the bottom, the subcopy is tiny, the can is jammed against the left and bottom edges, and the wide right half is dead space. B: '2 FOR' still sits below '$3', and the CTA and logo are tiny pills crammed together at bottom-left. The CTA is illegible and breaks the centred text axis. Still, B's headline, offer and subcopy form a coherent, readable block and the can is better framed, so it is the less broken of the two.

A reflows the two-line headline onto one line, which suits the strip, and keeps the bold serif at a size that fills the height with even margins, so the original's punchy feel survives; at most it could sit a touch larger. B uses the same one-line layout but shrinks the type so far that it floats small in a lot of dead space, which weakens the only focal element and drains the impact of this text-only design.

A is just the portrait original shrunk into the middle of the landscape canvas, with huge empty white side bands. It wasn't rearranged at all, and the logo and address text are tiny, but the hierarchy and grouping are intact. B does try a banner layout, but the reading order is broken: the 'EXHIBITION' kicker has dropped below the address. The date block floats off-axis to the right of the headline's left edge, the logo has shrunk to an illegible speck, and the image is cropped so hard that the concrete block motif is lost. The big empty right side makes it lopsided.

A: the oversized logo's 'MONOGRAPH' wordmark runs into the edge of the white panel. The 'Plan a Visit' CTA has shrunk to a tiny pill jammed against the bottom edge, and the 'NOW OPEN' eyebrow now sits after the CTA instead of above the headline. B is worse on reading order: the CTA sits above the headline and 'NOW OPEN' falls to the bottom. Its 'MONOGRAPH' wordmark also spills off the photo panel into the white, and the body line runs right up against the logo panel. A at least keeps headline, then body, then action.

A rearranges for the strip, but the reading order is wrong: the tiny 'Plan a Visit' pill sits alone at the top of the card above the headline, and the 'NOW OPEN' eyebrow drops to the bottom under the body copy. The oversized logo on the photo also competes with the headline. B is basically a shrunk copy of the original: the 'MONOGRAPH' wordmark under the logo is too small to read, the body copy is small, and the card nearly touches the top and bottom edges. Still, B keeps the original hierarchy and order (eyebrow, headline, copy, CTA) intact.

A actually rearranges the banner into a stacked square, but the logo is oversized and outweighs the small 'Three talks this week' headline. The leftover divider rules are stray: one runs from the logo's top edge to the right margin, and one cuts under the THU row. The list is indented off the headline's left edge, and 'All free, all at 19:00.' sits detached below the list. B is just the banner's three columns stretched vertically, with huge dead gaps between the TUE/WED/THU rows and between the headline and its subcopy. The logo is tiny with an illegible 'GALLERY' line, so it reads as a stretched banner rather than a composed design.

A: the white card fills almost the whole canvas, so the desert dunes that carry the original's mood shrink to a thin strip at the bottom. A huge empty white gap separates the subhead from a tiny See Fares button stranded bottom-left, and the centred logo clashes with the left-aligned copy. B: the card runs off the right edge with no margin, and See Fares is jammed against that edge beside the logo. That puts the CTA above the headline and breaks the reading order. Still, B keeps the text grouped, has a strong headline and shows more of the desert, so it is less broken than A's empty card.

A: the white card fills almost the whole canvas, so the desert imagery is reduced to a sliver along the bottom. The logo floats at an arbitrary x-position that doesn't line up with the left-aligned headline, the headline sits close to the left edge, and the small See Fares button is pushed against the far right edge, cut off from the copy. B keeps the desert backdrop and a centered card, but the logo straddles the card's top edge, the card runs into the bottom edge, and the See Fares CTA is shrunk to an illegible pill. A wins narrowly because its call to action is still readable.

A: the oversized Meridian logo straddles the top edge of the blue panel, half on the sky and half on the panel, which is a clear collision. The '40% OFF' badge is squashed into a flat, tiny ellipse that floats in the bottom-left. The panel bleeds off the left and bottom edges. Headline, copy and CTA do keep a sensible top-to-bottom order. B: the CTA and the squashed badge are jammed into the top-left corner, above the logo and headline, which breaks the reading order and hierarchy. The logo is so large it competes with the headline. The panel covers almost all of the beach scene, so most of the original imagery is lost, and the sunglasses sit awkwardly on the blue field.

A: the blue panel is jammed against the top and right canvas edges. The CTA and a tiny, unreadable 'UP TO 40% OFF' badge sit in the top corner above the headline, so the reading order is reversed and the CTA is buried. The logo is blown up huge on the busy horizon and leaves the left half as empty water. B keeps the right reading order (glasses, headline, copy, CTA at the bottom), but the panel bleeds off the bottom edge. The badge is squashed into a distorted, illegible ellipse, the oversized 'Meridian' logo runs into the panel edge, and 'sale' is orphaned on its own line. B is still the less broken of the two.

A squashes the round NEW badge into a flattened oval, which distorts a brand element. It also shrinks the jar to a small afterthought floating on a centre axis that matches nothing, while the text is left-aligned, so the product hero is lost and the stacking looks arbitrary. B keeps the original structure with the badge round and the jar at hero size, and the hierarchy reads clearly; its only flaws are minor: a little dead space on the right and the CTA sitting slightly tight to the bottom edge.

A: the CTA sits at x≈522 while the headline and subcopy start at x≈398, so the text column is broken; the NEW badge floats alone in the top-right corner, away from the jar; and the big, uneven gaps between headline, subcopy and button scatter the group, with a small headline lost in a lot of empty space. B: the badge, headline, subcopy and CTA share one left edge, which gives a clear column next to a well-sized jar. Its flaws: the headline is undersized for the canvas, the subcopy is tiny and low in contrast, the gap from subcopy to CTA is too large, and the badge has been moved off the product.

A: the circle is stretched into an ellipse. The 'Lumen & Fig' logo lockup has shrunk to a tiny cluster pressed against the left edge, so the brand is no longer the focal point and the tagline in the ellipse outranks it. The right third of the canvas is dead space, which makes the layout lopsided. B: the wordmark stays large and dominant, so the hierarchy is right, but the circle is also distorted into an ellipse and cropped off the right edge, the 'g' of 'Fig' collides with the ellipse's edge, and the tagline is small and pushed into the far corner.

A: the dark panel takes up almost the whole canvas and bleeds off the left and bottom edges, so the night-city scene is lost except for an odd sliver down the right edge. The centred logo clashes with the left-aligned text, the 'OBSIDIAN ONE' eyebrow drops below the body copy, and the headphones and CTA float in empty space inside the panel. B: it keeps the starry city and has a deliberate headphone overlap on the panel. However, the logo sits awkwardly off-centre top-right, the eyebrow is again below the body copy, the centred CTA doesn't match the left-aligned copy, and the headline and body run almost to the panel edges with tight margins.

A is basically the original scaled down. The card's hierarchy and reading order are intact, but the Monograph logo is shrunk to an illegible speck, the body copy is tiny with an orphaned 'entry.', and the card is cramped with little bottom padding. B breaks the reading order: the 'Plan a Visit' CTA sits above the headline, and the 'NOW OPEN' eyebrow drops below the body copy. Its oversized logo sits on the busy striped photo, and 'GALLERY' lands on a dark band. The logo also outweighs the headline as the focal point.

A scatters the four steps: step 3 sits above the headline, step 2 is under it, and steps 4 and 1 are dumped at the bottom below the CTA. The list's order and grouping are gone, and the left edges are ragged. B keeps the steps together in one aligned block under a strong headline, but they read in the wrong order (1, 3, 2, 4). B also shrinks the CTA into a small pill in the top-right corner, where it competes with the logo, and the jar is pushed tight against the bottom edge.

A: the $48 stays the hero, but the serum bottle is shrunk and pushed off to the left of an off-centre circle, and the $48 runs into the circle's edge. The cream jar ends up orphaned below the CTA, and 'THE NIGHT SET' now sits under its own supporting copy. B: the serum is a good size, but the $48 is shrunk to roughly body-copy size, so the price no longer stands out. The headline, copy, worth line and 'THE NIGHT SET' label are jammed together with a dead gap above the CTA, and the cream jar is a near-invisible speck off-axis at bottom-left. Both lose the product pairing. A keeps the price hierarchy better.

A stretches the circle into a full-bleed ellipse, pushes the logo mark against the left edge so it crosses the ellipse boundary, and inverts the hierarchy: the tagline is set larger than the 'Lumen & Fig' wordmark. B keeps the logo and wordmark dominant and in proportion, but the circle is still squashed into a cropped ellipse, the ellipse edge cuts through 'Fig', and the tagline is pushed off on its own to the far right.

A: the card fills the whole canvas, so the city-skyline image is almost entirely lost apart from a few star pixels. The 'OBSIDIAN ONE' eyebrow has dropped below the body copy, which breaks the reading order, and there is a large dead gap above the CTA. Still, the left edge is consistent and the hierarchy is clean. B: the 'OBSIDIAN ONE' eyebrow is moved below the body copy and enlarged into a wide-tracked cyan line that competes with the headline. The tiny right-aligned logo sits on an arbitrary axis, the centred CTA clashes with the left-aligned text, the headline and body are cramped together, and the card runs into a cropped city strip at the bottom that looks like an accident.

A: the earbud product is shrunk to a tiny thumbnail jammed near the left edge, so the hero image is trivialised. The whole content block sits in the upper two-thirds, leaving a dead band along the bottom, and the single-line headline makes the centre column feel thin. B: the product keeps real presence and the left/centre/right banner layout is better balanced vertically. But the case image looks soft and upscaled, the two-line headline in a wide strip wastes space, and the logo/headline/price stack is small next to the oversized product and CTA, so hierarchy competes.

A keeps the logo intact and legible, and its single-line headline reads clearly in a centred stack. But the earbud case is shrunk to a small icon that loses its role as the hero, the stack is tightly packed with little gap between the price and the undersized Shop button, and it reads as a squeezed vertical copy rather than a layout rearranged for the wider canvas. B's two-column split suits the shape and has a strong headline, but the Obsidian logo is shrunk to an illegible speck that no longer matches the original mark, and it sits loosely at the top right, off the text column's edge. The product also floats low on the left with dead space above it, so the brand is effectively lost.

A is broken. The headphones are cropped off the left edge, and the earbuds case is gone: only two stray dots and a pill-shaped plinth remain. The eyebrow now sits below the subhead, which flips the reading order. The price labels and the CTA are scattered, with 'Compare Models' sitting on a stray grey ellipse. B keeps a sensible left-to-right order: logo, eyebrow, headline, CTA on the left, products on the right. Its flaws: the logo and the subhead are tiny and hard to read, there is a large empty gap between the headline and the subhead, and the earbuds and their plinth are jammed against the right and bottom edges with the price label nearly clipped.

A: the quote mark, headline and copy are pushed to an arbitrary column near x≈135 that doesn't line up with the bottom-left logo, which leaves a dead left half. The tiny cyan attribution is jammed right under the headline, and 'Rated 5 out of 5' is bigger than the attribution, so the hierarchy is upside down. B: everything shares one clean left edge and the spacing is calmer. Its flaws: the headline wraps with an orphaned 'wear.' and is undersized for the canvas, the logo moved to the top so the reading order differs from the original, and 'Rated 5 out of 5' is very small.

A: the Shop button is pushed almost flush against the right edge (about 4px margin) and the logo sits close to the left edge, so the margins are uneven. The headline is also pulled left, which leaves a large dead gap before the CTA. B keeps the original's left-to-right rhythm with even margins of about 28px on both sides and a properly sized CTA. Its headline sits slightly off-centre between the logo and the button, and the spacing is a bit loose, but that only needs minor polish.

A: headline and Shop button share a left edge and the headline clearly leads, but the logo floats off-axis (neither centred nor on that left edge), the button is undersized, and there is dead space on the right with the button sitting low. B: the oversized logo competes with the headline for attention, and the elements use three different axes (logo left at ~18px, headline jammed near the left edge at ~10px, button roughly centred), so the layout looks arbitrary.

A gets the reading order wrong: the RSVP button sits above the headline and the 'LISTENING SESSION' label falls below the body copy. The date card is shrunk to a token and its 'FRI, 7:30 PM' is unreadable. The headphones are pulled off their grey circle, which is left as a stray blob in the bottom-right. B keeps the original order and a readable date card, but the headline, body and CTA are spread down the canvas with large dead gaps, and the body text is small. B's headphones are also pulled off the grey circle, leaving it stranded in the corner. Both need rework, but B is less broken.

A: the headline reads well and the order runs left to right, but the 'Grab a Can' CTA and the NEW FLAVOUR and ZERO SUGAR badges are tiny and barely legible. The yellow circle is cropped and crammed behind the logo in the top-right corner, and the far left of the banner is dead space. B: the yellow circle collides with the headline and covers 'here'. The FIZZBANG logo is oversized and competes with the headline, while the stacked badges and the CTA are shrunk until they cannot be read, so the action is lost.

A breaks the reading order: the 'Find a Store' CTA sits at the very top, the FIZZBANG! logo is pushed to the bottom, and '$3' comes before its '2 FOR' lead-in, which turns the offer into '$3 … 2 FOR'. It also leaves a large dead gap between $3 and the copy. B keeps the original logo → can → 2 FOR → $3 → copy → CTA order with even spacing and intact brand colours. B's only flaw is the orphaned 'long.' in the body copy, and since the aspect ratio is nearly the same, a close copy of the original layout is the right call here.

A: the headline is strong, but the date card has shrunk to a tiny chip where SAT/NOV/time can't be read. The 'FIZZBANG ARCADE NIGHT' kicker has dropped below the body copy, so the reading order is wrong. The pattern band is squashed into a thin strip that floats above the CTA, and the controller is shrunk and stranded at the bottom, leaving the column scattered and loose. B: the composition and hierarchy are much more deliberate, with the pattern block on the left, a big headline and a prominent CTA. But the date card and the kicker are shrunk to microscopic, illegible size next to the logo, so the event date is effectively lost. The body copy is also small and crammed beside the controller.

A keeps a sensible order (headline, then copy, controller, can, CTA), but the FIZZBANG logo pill at the bottom is blown up so big that it competes with the headline. The can is shrunk to a tiny afterthought, the CTA button is small and crammed under it, and there is dead space between the copy and the controller. B puts the CTA above the headline, which breaks the reading order. Its body copy is almost as large as the headline, which flattens the hierarchy and wraps the copy into short ragged lines. The logo and can are tiny and squeezed into the bottom-left corner, so the brand is nearly lost, and the bottom of the canvas is empty.

A: the white panel takes up almost the whole strip and the pop-art shapes shrink to a sliver, so the brand feel is mostly gone. The FIZZBANG pill is jammed against the left edge on top of shape fragments, and the oversized CTA competes with the headline. B keeps a readable cluster of the original shapes (pink circle, navy quarter, yellow bar) with the logo layered over them, and the headline clearly leads a subordinate CTA. However, the CTA is crammed against the right edge, there is a gap between the headline and the CTA, and the logo sits awkwardly across the boundary between the shapes and the panel.

A: the FIZZBANG badge sits half over the busy pink/navy/yellow graphic strip and butts right against the headline with no gap, the CTA is jammed against the headline and the right edge, and the CTA label is tiny. The cluster is cramped and has no breathing room. B: spacing is more even and every text element is readable, but the oversized logo badge also sits on top of the busy shapes, and the headline is now smaller than both the logo and the large CTA, so the hierarchy is inverted. A thin blue sliver is left dangling at the right edge.

A: the FIZZBANG logo pill sits on top of a busy pink, yellow and blue shape cluster crammed into the left corner. The headline breaks to leave 'can' alone on its own line, and the CTA is tiny and hard to read at 320x50; most of the pop-art graphics and the white card are gone. B has the same orphaned 'can' and a logo that is clipped against the left edge over the busy shapes, but its headline and CTA are bigger and more legible, and the left-to-right banner reading order is cleaner, so it is slightly less bad.

A drops all of the original's pop-art geometry: the blue field, circles, stripes and triangles are gone, leaving a plain white page. It also puts the FIZZBANG! logo below the headline, which flips the original reading order, and leaves large dead gaps between the headline, logo and CTA. A cropped blue/teal strip sits jammed against the bottom edge and reads as an accident. B also loses all of the brand's background graphics, so it barely looks like the same design. However, it keeps the original order (logo, headline, CTA), and the headline is bold and dominant. Its weaker points are a cramped top margin above the logo and an empty, unbranded canvas.

A rearranges for the banner, with a large FIZZBANG pill on the left and the badge on the right, so it reads left to right with a dominant wordmark. But the pill crowds the top, bottom and left edges, and the tiny SINCE 2026 badge floats mid-right with no clear alignment and dead space beyond it. B is a shrunk, centred copy of the square: the logo pill fills only about a fifth of the width, the badge text is tiny, and both sides are empty halftone, so it doesn't fit the format and the brand loses its impact.

A keeps the original's two-line centred break and plenty of whitespace around it, so the calm 'silence' feel survives. The headline is a bit small for the banner and the layout is close to a plain shrink, which is minor polish. B re-flows the line to one row, which suits a banner, but the headline runs almost to the left and right edges (about 15px margins). That leaves it cramped from side to side, with empty bands above and below, which goes against the original's generous breathing room.

A is centred and keeps the font, but it blows the headline up into a shouting three-line stack, one word per line. The side margins get tight around 'silence.' and the quiet, airy minimalism of the original is gone, which goes against the message itself. B keeps the original's two-line wrap and scale, but the block sits well below centre (its middle is at about y≈495 on a 768px canvas), with a large dead area above and a cramped bottom margin. It looks like a placement error, not a deliberate choice.

A: the image-left/text-right split works for a banner, but the date box is indented and not aligned with the headline's left edge. The 'EXHIBITION' kicker has dropped below the venue line, so the reading order is reversed. The logo is shrunk to an unreadable speck, and the right third of the canvas is dead space. B: the headline is bold and dominant, but it nearly butts against a narrowly cropped image that loses the original's architecture. The date box floats in the top right with illegible micro-text ('Tuesday to Sunday…'). The logo, venue and 'EXHIBITION' are jammed into one tiny run along the bottom, so the hierarchy and grouping fall apart.

A: the date block is shrunk to an unreadable sliver and sits above the headline. The EXHIBITION eyebrow, address and logo are crammed into one microscopic row at the bottom, there is a big dead area on the left, and the image floats right with uneven margins. B: the headline and the date/hours block are readable and the image keeps its proportions, but the date block is indented and doesn't share the headline's left edge. The headline is jammed against the top, the EXHIBITION eyebrow has dropped below the address, and the logo is shrunk to an illegible speck, so the brand is effectively lost.

A: the quote is squeezed onto one tiny line, so the message is close to unreadable. The oversized Monograph logo takes over the frame and flips the hierarchy, and the quote mark has shrunk to almost nothing. B is worse: the attribution 'AIKO TANABE, ARCHITECT' is set wider and heavier than the quote itself. B's tiny one-line quote also runs nearly edge to edge with almost no side margins, and 'GALLERY' under the logo has faded to illegible.

A: the logo is blown up to fill the top 70%, which buries the headline and talk list in a cramped bottom strip. The list is indented and doesn't line up with the headline, 'All free, all at 19:00.' is stranded below the list, out of reading order and jammed against the edge, and leftover divider lines float at the top right and bottom. B: this is the landscape banner stretched to the taller shape rather than rearranged. The three talks are spread about 180px apart with no grouping, the headline and the 'All free' line are separated by dead space, and the logo is tiny. Two orphaned rules and huge empty areas leave the layout unusable.

A: the stacked story order works and the logo reads clearly, but the logo is far bigger than the content and outweighs the headline. The headline and talk list are small and packed into one band with empty space above and below, the list is indented off the headline's left edge, the divider rules are lost, and two stray lines are left at the top and bottom. B: this is the landscape layout stretched to a tall shape. The logo is tiny (the GALLERY text is unreadable), the headline, the 'All free' note and the three talk rows are scattered far apart down the canvas, all the text is too small for a story, and the stray rules and huge empty gaps make it look unplanned.

A: the CTA is a tiny pill crammed into the top-right corner next to the sunglasses, so it gets buried and reads first instead of last. The light-blue circle has come loose from the suitcase and sits as a stray blob in the bottom-right, and the logo is jammed near the bottom edge. B: the reading order works better (headline, then copy, then product, then CTA), but the CTA is very small and pushed down in the bottom-left. A large empty band sits between the suitcase and the CTA, and the blue circle is again an orphan blob in the bottom-right corner.

A is unusable. The fare cards are shrunk to tiny slivers with unreadable text, scattered down the canvas and out of order. The subline floats alone, and the headline sits near the bottom below its own supporting copy, with large dead gaps throughout. B keeps the cards readable but has clear flaws. The CTA is a tiny pill crammed into the top-right corner, losing its prominence. The card stack is out of order (Marrakech, Reykjavik, Lisbon). The cards are jammed right under the headline and sit off-centre against the left-aligned text. The subline is stranded below the cards, and the logo is inset unevenly.

A keeps the four steps together as one list, but they read in the wrong order (1, 3, 2, 4). The CTA is shrunk into a small pill in the top-right corner, where it competes with the logo instead of closing the reading path, and the steps are tight against the jar. B breaks the numbered list apart: step 3 sits above the headline, step 2 is stranded under it, and steps 4 and 1 hang below the CTA in reverse order. The list order is destroyed, the steps have no grouping and the reading flow is incoherent, so B is unusable.

A keeps the structure (copy left, products right) but everything is tiny: the logo, eyebrow, body copy and price labels are close to illegible. The left column is ragged too: the logo and CTA sit at about x80 while the headline and body start at about x124. The headphones have lost their base ellipse, and the buds' ellipse runs off the right edge. B is broken: the headphones are cropped at the left canvas edge, the buds have shrunk to two stray dots, and the price labels float away from their products. The eyebrow 'Pick your sound' sits below the headline, and the CTA is dumped bottom-right on a stray grey blob.

A: the logo is blown up until it rivals or beats the headline, so there are two competing focal points. The Shop button floats off-centre (around x 118–183) and lines up with neither the left-aligned headline nor the canvas centre, and the large gap under the logo looks unplanned. B: the headline and CTA share a clean left edge and the headline clearly leads. However, the logo is indented (about x 58) instead of sitting on that same left edge, the CTA is small for its role, and the bottom-right is left empty, so it needs polish before shipping.

A: headline and CTA are strong and well grouped, but the date card (the key event info) is shrunk to an unreadable icon next to the logo. The eyebrow is microscopic, a blown-up crop of the decorative strip fills almost half the canvas, and the body copy is cramped and tiny beside the controller. B: the date card is again tiny and its time line can't be read. The reading order is jumbled, with the eyebrow placed under the body copy, and the decorative strip is crushed into a thin broken sliver. Left-aligned and centred elements are mixed with no shared axis, and the controller is a trivial speck, so the whole thing looks like scattered fragments.

A is just a shrunk, centred copy: the FIZZBANG! pill covers about a fifth of the banner width, and the SINCE 2026 badge is tiny and hard to read. Most of the canvas is enlarged halftone dots, so the brand is lost in the pattern. B gives the logo pill a confident size and reads left to right, but the pill sits tight against the left edge. The badge floats in the middle-right, away from the logo, and the right third is empty, so the layout is lopsided and needs work on spacing and grouping.

A has a clean headline-to-CTA hierarchy and the CTA has room around it, but the Lumen & Fig logo has shrunk to an illegible speck in the bottom-left, the 'NEW NIGHT SERUM' eyebrow falls below the body copy (wrong reading order), and the bottle crowds the card edge. B jams the 'Shop the Serum' button right up against the end of the headline so they nearly collide, and the eyebrow is tiny, low-contrast text pushed into a footer beside the logo. B's logo stays readable, but the headline/CTA crowding is the worse flaw.

A: a sensible left-to-right banner with a clear headline and CTA. But the 'NEW NIGHT SERUM' eyebrow sits below the body copy, which breaks the reading order. The logo is pushed to the bottom of the card, with the fig icon clipped by the card edge. The card runs almost to the top and bottom of the canvas, so it feels cramped. B: the Lumen & Fig logo has shrunk to an unreadable few pixels and fallen outside the card onto the leaves, so the brand is effectively lost. The bottle is cut off at the bottom of the canvas. The eyebrow also sits below the body copy, and the card floats at the top with an empty strip of leaves underneath.

A: the headline breaks badly, leaving 'duo' alone on the second line. The CTA is indented off the text column's left edge and overlaps a stray peach circle in the corner. The serum bottle has shrunk to a tiny isolated sprite at the bottom, cut off from the jar, which breaks up the 'duo' product pair. There is also a lot of dead space at the top left and between blocks. B: the order of headline, subline, product and then CTA is clean, and the headline sits on one line. However, the logo is centred above left-aligned text. The serum bottle has shrunk to an almost invisible sliver under the CTA. The peach circle sits empty in the bottom-right corner, leaving the bottom unbalanced. B reads a little more deliberately than A.

A: the steps are out of order (1, 3, 2, 4). Step 4 is smaller and indented off the shared left edge. The CTA is shrunk and pushed up beside the logo, where it competes with the brand. The jar is oversized and dominates the right half. B is worse: steps 2–4 are scattered down the far-left edge at a tiny, unreadable size, and their badge numbers look wrong. Step 1 is cut off from the rest of the list and sits at the bottom next to the CTA. The headline is huge while the list falls apart, so the reading order is lost.

A is just a shrunken copy in the middle of a big empty canvas: the logo, the four step lines and the CTA label are too small to read, the elements are scattered with no shared grid, and the jar and circle are pushed into the bottom-right corner. B makes good use of the wide format, with a large jar on the left and a strong one-line headline, but it is still broken: the steps run out of order (1, 3, 2), step 4 shrinks to unreadable fine print, the peach circle runs into the step 3 and step 2 text, and the CTA is pressed against the top-right edge.

A: the jar is a strong hero on the left and the headline block reads in order, but the NEW badge has shrunk to an unreadable dot floating above the headline. The subcopy is tiny. Shop Now floats alone at the far right, with a big dead gap between it and the text. B: the jar is shrunk and crammed to the left edge. The NEW badge is orphaned below the subcopy near the bottom edge, so the reading order is wrong, and it is illegible. The CTA is stranded far right across a large empty middle, which leaves the layout lopsided and weak.

A keeps the original structure intact: the quote mark sits next to the headline, the attribution, CTA and logo stack in order, and the bottle and circle stay to the right. Its flaws are small: the Lumen & Fig logo is tiny and floats low, and there's slack space at the bottom. B breaks up the layout. The quote mark is stranded far above its quote, which drops to the bottom edge under a large empty band. The 'Read 2,400 Reviews' CTA is pushed into the top-right corner, crowding the bottle cap and away from its copy. The attribution is jammed against the bottom edge, and the reading order is scrambled.

A: the order is right (logo, then tagline), but the 'Lumen & Fig' wordmark is shrunk to about 6px and can't be read, while the tagline dominates. That reverses the original hierarchy, and the ellipse is awkwardly clipped at the left edge. B is worse on the same problems: the tagline comes before the brand, and the tiny logo and wordmark are jammed against the period and the right edge of the ellipse with no gap, so they read as an afterthought.

A is a clean left-to-right banner, but the earbud case is shrunk to a small icon on the far left. The logo floats alone at the top centre, a loose gap separates the headline from the price line, and the canvas is mostly empty dark space. B gives the product real weight and groups logo, headline and price into one tight block, so it is more balanced and closer to the original. Its flaws: the headline and the price line (about 9px) are small and weak next to the oversized product, and the CTA sits slightly higher than the text block.

A keeps a clean vertical stack, but the CTA has shrunk to a tiny pill in the top-right corner sitting on the circle, so it is buried. The stat order is shuffled, the tagline has dropped below the stats, and the legal line is set as large as body copy. B is broken: the stats are scattered across the whole canvas ('40 h' and 'BT 5.4' crammed around the tagline above the headline, '-38 dB' under the CTA, '6 mics' at the very bottom). The tagline sits above its own headline and the small text sits on the circle graphic, so there is no grouping and no reading order.

A: the CTA sits above the headline, so the reading order is backwards. The FIZZBANG logo and the can are shrunk to tiny, illegible marks at the bottom, which trivialises the brand, and the oversized controller dominates the left. B: the CTA is also above the headline and pushed tight to the top-right corner, and a large dead gap separates the subcopy from the logo and can. Still, B's logo and can stay legible and in proportion, and its headline and subcopy have better line lengths.

A keeps the logo legible, centred above the headline. But the flavour list is small, its dots step out of line row by row, and the order is reshuffled (Lime Zap moved last). The CTA is a tiny button with illegible text, cut off from everything at the bottom-left, which leaves a large dead area on the left. B makes the headline and list larger and easier to read. But it shrinks the FIZZBANG! logo to an illegible chip in the top-left corner, which hurts the brand, and moves the tiny CTA to the top-right, where it is read before the headline. The list in B is also ragged (Lime Zap's dot is offset) and reordered, and the lower-left is empty.

A keeps the headline and subline together in the centre, but the can is shrunk to a tiny strip that loses its role as the hero, there is dead space on the left, and the yellow circle is a cropped scrap jammed behind the CTA's top-right corner. B has the same circle scrap colliding with the CTA, and it is worse: the can is jammed against the left and top edges and is barely readable, and the subline sits far below the headline, tiny and almost touching the bottom edge, so the copy no longer reads as one group.

A: the can is tiny and pushed flush against the left edge, the subhead is small and sits far below the headline, which breaks up the copy block, and the yellow circle (the brand motif) has become a cropped blob stuck to the oversized CTA's corner. B fixes the copy grouping and gives the can some room from the edge, but it repeats the stray cropped circle behind the CTA, the can is still small, and there are wide empty gaps between the can, the copy and the button.

A keeps the original's centred, quiet composition: the headline is restacked into three centred lines that fill the narrow width well. Its only weakness is that the 'Form / follows / silence.' break leaves 'Form' short and a little isolated. B shrinks the headline and drops it into the lower half (top at ~55%), so the upper half is lopsided dead space and the original's calm centred balance is lost.

A turns the two-line headline into one line, centred on both axes, set at a confident size with even side margins, so it suits the strip format. The only polish needed: the headline is a little small for the canvas height, leaving thin space above and below. B sets the headline noticeably smaller and off-centre: it sits about 35px left of the horizontal centre and is pushed into the top third. That leaves a large dead band underneath, so it looks like a misplaced paste rather than an intentional layout.

A rewraps the headline onto one line for the banner, keeps its weight, and centres it vertically. The only flaw is that the side margins are a little tight for the minimal, quiet feel of the original. B keeps the portrait two-line break, so the headline is small and swamped by empty space on both sides. It also sits low in the frame, with roughly 60px above and 35px below, so it reads as a shrunk copy rather than a layout made for the banner.

A properly reflows for the tall format with a strong two-line headline, but the 'EXHIBITION' eyebrow has been dropped below the address, which breaks the reading order. The address is also set bigger than the date/hours line, the hours text inside the black box is tiny, the inset photo loses the original full-bleed, and the bottom is dead space under a small left-aligned logo. B keeps the original order but reads as a shrunk copy floating mid-canvas, with an unexplained white band above the photo and a large empty bottom third. Its eyebrow, address and logo are tiny, and the one-line headline is undersized for the format.

A keeps the schedule as one readable block beside the image, but it is clearly broken. The dates are out of order (02 DEC, then 13/20 JAN, then 16 DEC, 06 JAN, 09 DEC). The legal line sits wedged inside the list. The 'WINTER PROGRAMME' kicker has dropped below the list, and the logo is a speck under the CTA. B is unusable. Several rows (beside the CTA, by the headline, bottom right) are microscopic and unreadable, the order is jumbled, and the legal line and a schedule row are jammed together along the bottom edge.

A breaks the design: the schedule is out of date order (02 DEC, 13 JAN, 20 JAN, 16 DEC…), the legal line sits between two schedule rows, the WINTER PROGRAMME eyebrow has moved below the list, and the logo is shrunk and buried at the bottom. B keeps the original structure, but its left edges don't line up: the logo is at about x62, the eyebrow and headline at 51, the rows at 58 and the button at 46. The times and the image also end on different right edges, and the headline still wraps to an orphaned 'studios'.

A scrambles the content: the dated schedule is out of order (02 Dec, then 13 Jan, 20 Jan, 16 Dec, 06 Jan, 09 Dec), the legal line sits between the first and second list rows, the 'WINTER PROGRAMME' eyebrow lands below the list, the list is crammed tight under the headline, and the logo is pushed to the bottom where its wordmark is cut off. B keeps the original structure and reading order, but it is basically a narrowed copy: the logo, list text and CTA are small for the tall format, the list rows are spaced out, and there is dead space between the CTA and the fine print, so it needs a proper vertical re-layout before it ships.

A drops the sea photo entirely, a real fidelity loss, and leaves typographic orphans: '$89' sits alone on its own line, 'Sunday.' is orphaned and the headline is broken into three lines. Even so, it keeps a clean shared left edge and a clear headline → copy → CTA order. B shrinks the photo to a meaningless sliver at the bottom, pushes the logo to the right so it no longer lines up with the left-aligned copy, packs the text into the top third, leaves a large dead blue gap in the middle, and centres the CTA, which breaks the grid.

A has a clear left-to-right banner flow: image, then headline and subcopy aligned on one left edge, then the CTA. But the crop shows a green hill, not the original sea and sky. The small white Meridian logo sits on that busy image with weak contrast, and the Book Now button is pushed almost against the right edge. B's oversized logo straddles the image/blue-panel boundary, so 'Meridian' crosses the seam and sits half on the busy photo, which is an unwanted collision. Its subcopy is tiny next to a huge CTA that competes with the headline, and the CTA is crammed toward the bottom-right with an odd sliver of blue beyond it.

A: the white card runs past the left and right canvas edges, so its corners get cut off. The logo floats indented at about x=155 and doesn't line up with the headline's left edge. A large dead gap separates the logo from the headline. The CTA sits alone in the top-right corner, away from its copy. The desert imagery is cut down to a thin strip. B: the logo rides up over the card's top edge, so it collides with the boundary and sits on the background. The 'See Fares' CTA has shrunk to an unreadable pill stranded at the bottom. A big empty gap opens below the subhead, and 'away' is left as an orphan. B does keep the dunes and reads as a better left-to-right split, but its illegible CTA and logo collision are worse than A's misalignment.

A uses the landscape format sensibly: copy column on the left, large suitcase on the right. But the copy reads '$199 / New York / from', which breaks the original's 'New York from $199' order and leaves 'from' dangling above the CTA. The Meridian logo is shrunk to an illegible footnote, and the suitcase wheels sit almost on the bottom edge. B is a narrow centred stack with the same broken order. Its 'from' jams against the suitcase handle, the Book button crowds or overlaps the suitcase wheels, the suitcase is shrunk, both sides of the canvas are dead space, and the logo is a tiny orphan in the bottom-left corner.

A: the Meridian logo is blown up to a giant wordmark that outweighs the headline as the focal point. The 'Up to 40% off' badge has shrunk to an illegible sticker, the CTA is undersized, and the panel bleeds off the right and bottom edges. B: the logo butts against the panel edge (the 'n' touches the blue box) and the headline leaves 'sale' orphaned on its own line.
